body.title: Serialized map restore retains old keys and ignores JSON decode errors
body.body:
## My urfave/cli version is

Current v3 `main`, commit `d5c06cb04479eeacbbb9378ea26261b6be516320`. Reproduced with `go version go1.26.6 linux/amd64`.

## Checklist

- Tested current main, not claiming this was checked against every release.
- [x] Searched existing issues and PRs. The slice work in #2524 is separate.

## Describe the bug

`MapBase.Set`'s prefixed serialized path calls `json.Unmarshal` into the existing map and discards the returned error. Although the source comment says deserialization assumes overwrite, keys missing from a later saved map remain present. Restoring an empty object does not clear the map. A wrong JSON value type for a string-map entry can leave a zero string and still run the command action without an error.

## To reproduce

Run this in a module using current main:

```go
package main

import (
 "context"
 "encoding/json"
 "fmt"
 "strings"
 cli "github.com/urfave/cli/v3"
)

func main() {
 prefix := strings.TrimSuffix(cli.NewStringMap(nil).Serialize(), "null")
 cases := []struct{name, value string}{
  {"new map", cli.NewStringMap(map[string]string{"new":"two"}).Serialize()},
  {"empty map", cli.NewStringMap(map[string]string{}).Serialize()},
  {"wrong value type", prefix + `{"bad":42}`},
 }
 for _, tc := range cases {
  called := false
  cmd := &cli.Command{Flags: []cli.Flag{&cli.StringMapFlag{Name:"labels"}}, Action:func(ctx context.Context, cmd *cli.Command)error{
   called = true
   data, err := json.Marshal(cmd.StringMap("labels")); if err != nil{return err}
   fmt.Printf("%s: %s\n",tc.name,data);return nil
  }}
  err := cmd.Run(context.Background(), []string{"app","--labels",cli.NewStringMap(map[string]string{"old":"one"}).Serialize(),"--labels",tc.value})
  fmt.Printf("action=%t error=%v\n",called,err)
 }
}
```

## Observed behavior

```text
new map: {"new":"two","old":"one"}
action=true error=<nil>
empty map: {"old":"one"}
action=true error=<nil>
wrong value type: {"bad":"","old":"one"}
action=true error=<nil>
```

## Expected behavior / compatibility question

Should serialized map values replace the previous contents and reject malformed JSON or wrong-type values, rather than merge and ignore decode errors?

A tested private change decodes into a temporary map, checks the error, then assigns through the existing destination pointer. That would remove keys absent from a successful restore and return errors for invalid serialized values. Ordinary `key=value` parsing would be unchanged. The code remains private pending agreement on the semantics.

There is an additional compatibility choice: successful restore would replace the map value. The `Destination` pointer would remain connected, but aliases to the old map would no longer observe subsequent restores. Must those aliases keep observing restores? If so, would validating into a temporary map and then replacing the existing map's contents in place be preferred?

This is limited to the map path, not the slice deserialization work in #2524. It is not a blanket backward-compatibility claim or a proposed release classification.

body.title: fix: make bash completion work without bash-completion
body.body:
## What type of PR is this?

- bug

## What this PR does / why we need it:

On bash without the bash-completion package (stock macOS, minimal containers), the generated script runs `__<app>_init_completion -n "=:" || return`. The fallback calls `_comp_initialize` or `_get_comp_words_by_ref`, and when neither exists it fails, so the function returns before producing any completion: Tab prints `bash: _get_comp_words_by_ref: command not found` and offers nothing. The docs suggest `source <(app completion bash)`, so this is the documented path.

Since the request is built from `COMP_WORDS`/`COMP_CWORD` and `COMPREPLY` is initialized by the caller, the helper's only remaining effect was its `=:` word splitting. This deletes the helper and its call, and keeps that filter behavior with a local `cur="${cur##*[=:]}"`, so bash-completion users see no change and the script depends only on core bash builtins.

## Which issue(s) this PR fixes:

N/A — no matching upstream issue found.

## Special notes for your reviewer:

Dropping `_init_completion || return` also drops bash-completion's variable/redirect expansion for arguments like `$var` or `${arr[...]`; the registration's `-o bashdefault -o default` still offers filename/variable-expanded completion, so this is a niche behavior change. The new test covers plain bash and the `--flag=value` filter.

## Testing

`TestCompletionBashWithoutBashCompletion` evals the generated script under `bash --noprofile --norc` with `_init_completion`, `_comp_initialize` and `_get_comp_words_by_ref` unset, completes `--verb` to `--verbose`, and checks `--format=po` still filters to `port`. It fails with `command not found` on the old script. `go test ./...`, `go test -tags urfave_cli_no_template ./...`, `go vet ./...` and gofmt pass.

## Release Notes

```release-note
Bash completion now works when the bash-completion package is not installed, as on stock macOS bash 3.2.
```

AI assistance: implemented with Claude Code; the account owner reviewed the change.

body.title: perf: build flag names with one allocation
body.body:
## What type of PR is this?

- cleanup

## What this PR does / why we need it:

`FlagNames` built a temporary slice of the name and the aliases, and then appended to a slice with no capacity. Now it allocates the result once. Setup calls `FlagNames` many times through `Names()`, so each `Run` makes fewer allocations. The output does not change.

| Benchmark | Before | After | Allocs |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| `FlagNames`, 1 alias | 171 ns | 85 ns | 3 → 1 |
| `FlagNames`, 10 aliases | 575 ns | 208 ns | 6 → 1 |
| `Run`, 30 flags and 10 subcommands | 131 µs | 107 µs | 1807 → 1425 |
| `Run` a subcommand with flags | 184 µs | 146 µs | 2783 → 2067 |

## Which issue(s) this PR fixes:

None.

## Testing

- `make vet`, `make lint`, `make test` (also with `urfave_cli_no_template`), `make v3diff` and `make check-binary-size` pass.
- Old and new `Run` output, errors and flag values matched on 1M random apps and arguments.
- I measured no slowdown on AMD EPYC 7763 (Go 1.27.4, 24 interleaved rounds, 3 code layouts).

## Release Notes

```release-note
NONE
```

body.title: fix: do not suggest a hidden help command
body.body:
## What type of PR is this?

- bug

## What this PR does / why we need it:

`suggestCommand` adds `help` and `h` to the names of every command it looks at:

```go
for _, name := range append(command.Names(), helpName, helpAlias) {
```

When the help command is visible it is already in the command list, so the append changes nothing. When it is hidden (`HideHelpCommand` or `HideHelp`), the function can return a command that does not exist.

With `PrefixMatchCommands` this stops a real command from running:

```go
cmd := &cli.Command{
	Name:                "app",
	PrefixMatchCommands: true,
	HideHelpCommand:     true,
	Commands:            []*cli.Command{{Name: "hello", Action: ...}},
}
cmd.Run(ctx, []string{"app", "hel"})
// No help topic for 'hel'
```

`suggestCommand` returns `help` for `hel` (and `h` for `h`), `Command("help")` finds nothing, and `hello` is not run.

- `suggestions.go`: iterate over `command.Names()` only.
- `suggestions_test.go`: one test for `suggestCommand` without a help command in the list, one for the `PrefixMatchCommands` + `HideHelpCommand` run.

`suggestFlag` already takes a `hideHelp` argument for the same reason.

## Which issue(s) this PR fixes:

None, I did not find an existing issue for this.

## Testing

Both new tests fail on `main` (`expected: "hello"`, `actual: "help"`) and pass with the change. `go test ./...` passes. I did not run `make` (no `gfmrun` installed); the change does not touch the public API.

## Release Notes

```release-note
Hidden help command is no longer suggested or prefix-matched in place of a real command.
```

body.title: fix: do not print the version for --version=false
body.body:
## What type of PR is this?

- bug

## What this PR does / why we need it:

`checkVersion` only asks whether the version flag was set, not what it was set to:

```go
return cmd.versionFlag != nil && cmd.versionFlag.IsSet()
```

So `app --version=false` (or `-v=false`) prints the version and the action does not run. `checkHelp` reads the value of the help flag, so `--help=false` runs the action as expected.

- `help.go`: `checkVersion` returns false when the version flag is a bool flag set to false. A custom `VersionFlag` that is not a bool keeps the current `IsSet` behaviour.
- `command_test.go`: `TestCommand_Run_VersionFalse` covers `--version=false` and `-v=false`.

## Which issue(s) this PR fixes:

None, I did not find an existing issue for this.

## Testing

The new test fails on `main` (`expected: "boom I say!"`, `actual: "boom version 0.1.0\n"`) and passes with the change. `go test ./...` passes. I did not run `make` (no `gfmrun` installed); the change does not touch the public API.

## Release Notes

```release-note
`--version=false` no longer prints the version.
```
